label: Ilsa Roon's first greeting — introductions by name

purpose.value: Ilsa welcomes the hero with genuine warmth and tries to give the realms' people back their personhood — families, cultures, memories, ten thousand years of peace — one offered name at a time.

emotionalProgression.note: She likes people on principle and offers the hero the benefit of every doubt, once more.
She approaches the hard sentence the long way around: names, daughters, hearths — then says it plainly.
He hears 'they were defending their children' as 'they are breeding an army' and departs encouraged; she stays seated with the names.

notes: Misunderstanding pair (Lore.md): 'They were defending their children' → 'They are breeding an army.' She KNOWS the book is a children's comedy and can say so; he hears a clever disguise over forbidden prophecy. Her moral boundary holds in every state: she never dehumanizes him back — he is wrong, never a monster. Never validate the hero's prophecy framing: there is no canon fact supporting 'the realms are evil', and that absence is itself the guard.
